Below-normal rainfall is not expected to favour psyllid population growth but may increase mite populations, including vectors of Citrus Leprosis Virus. Conditions are also not expected to favour an increase in Drunken Bayman populations.

Below-normal rainfall may reduce flushing and stress trees. Dry, dusty conditions can increase mite pressure and may also favour scale insects and mealybugs on stressed trees. Asian citrus psyllid (ACP) pressure may be localized but can increase quickly wherever new flushing occurs.
Conditions may favour psyllid population growth. Rainfall is not expected to favour increased mite populations but may favour an increase in Drunken Bayman populations.
Rainfall during this period will benefit established orchards. Continue monitoring for pest and disease problems and implement appropriate control measures.

Avocado: Conditions may favour thrips, scales, red spider mites, mealybugs, and other pests. Drought stress may increase susceptibility to bacterial canker, stem blight, and leaf blight.
Avocado: Continue monitoring for thrips, scales, red spider mites, mealybugs, bacterial canker, stem blight, and leaf blight.
Avocado: Monitor for thrips, red spider mites, scales, and mealybugs. Fruit scarring, leaf bronzing, and fruit drop may increase in stressed trees.
Avocado: Monitor for thrips, scales, red spider mites, and mealybugs. Fruit scarring and leaf bronzing are more likely during hot, dry periods.

Below normal rainfall will reduce soil moisture and increase heat stress. These conditions may reduce flushing and flowering, increase fruit drop, reduce fruit size, and trigger outbreaks of mites, thrips, mealybugs, and scales.
Cacao: Drought stress may reduce flowering and pod development. If rainfall occurs in bursts, black pod disease may still develop where sanitation is poor.
Cacao: High humidity may continue to favour disease development.
Cacao: High humidity may favour disease development.

Cacao: Periods of rainfall and high humidity may favour black pod disease (Phytophthora) and other fungal diseases. Dry and hot conditions may cause stress and reduced flowering in young cacao plants.
Coconut: Conditions may favour coconut weevils, mites, red spider mites, Phytophthora, and Red Ring disease.
Coconut: Continue monitoring for coconut weevils, mites, red spider mites, Phytophthora, and Red Ring disease.
Coconut: Monitor for coconut weevils, rhinoceros beetles where present, red palm mites, spider mites, scales, and mealybugs.
Coconut: Monitor for red spider mites, red palm mites, scales, and mealybugs. Palms may weaken under prolonged moisture stress.
Coconut: coconut weevil/rhinoceros beetle (where present), red palm mite / spider mites, scale/mealybugs
Low rainfall and high temperatures may stress plants. Monitor for pest problems and implement appropriate control measures.
Other damage: Birds, rodents, and other mammals, including squirrels, may cause increased fruit damage during dry periods.
Other pest damage may include birds, rodents, and squirrels.
Pineapple: Conditions may favour sunscald of fruits, mealybugs, and stink bugs.
Pineapple: Continue monitoring for sunscald and other pest-related damage.
Pineapple: Monitor for sunscald, mealybugs, mealybug wilt, and stink bug damage. Fruit quality may decline under prolonged heat and moisture stress.
Pineapple: Monitor for sunscald, mealybugs, mealybug wilt, and stink bugs. Heat stress may reduce fruit quality.

Rainfall is expected to be adequate for production, but periods of low rainfall and high temperatures can still cause heat and moisture stress, especially on sandy or shallow soils and young trees. Stress can trigger outbreaks of mites, thrips, mealybugs, scales, and borers and increase the risk of sunscald in coconut, pineapple, and avocado. Tree stress can also predispose plants to cankers and dieback.
Soursop: Conditions may favour fruit, stem, and trunk borers, mealybugs, aphids, mites, thrips, scales, lacewings, defoliating caterpillars, and Anthracnose resulting from secondary insect damage.
Soursop: Continue monitoring for fruit, stem, and trunk borers, mealybugs, aphids, mites, thrips, scales, lacewings, defoliating caterpillars, and Anthracnose.

Soursop: Monitor for fruit, stem, and trunk borers, mealybugs, aphids, mites, thrips, scales, and secondary Anthracnose on damaged fruit.
